review_basis: Bounded taxonomy dependency review against retained, previously primary-text-reviewed source propositions and exact current classes. No fresh external-source verification or equivalence claim.

relationships.external_proposition: When the complete statutory critical incident trigger is satisfied for a covered asset and its responsible entity, give ASD an incident report including information prescribed by the rules, as soon as practicable and in any event within 12 hours after the entity becomes so aware. The initial report may be oral or written; if written, use the approved form.
relationships.fc_property: The property by which material decisions, requests, delegations and actions traverse required governance controls or review routes before reaching execution or another governed state, including validated route equivalence for direct, alternate, fallback, asynchronous, tool-mediated and cross-runtime paths.
relationships.invariant: Conduct subject to a required governance route may reach execution only through that route or an authorised equivalent preserving the same control effect. Direct, alternate, fallback, delegated, asynchronous, tool-mediated, and cross-runtime paths require route-equivalence validation before proceeding.
relationships.supported_component: The legally required incident report must traverse the prescribed ASD recipient route with its source-defined form and timing conditions.

actor: Responsible entity for an asset to which Part 2B applies, as defined by the actual asset class and s12L
conditions: Part 2B must apply to the asset under s30BB: the applicable rules or a s51 declaration, subject to any s30BB(3) / Application Rules r5(5) grace period.
The asset and responsible entity must satisfy ss9 and 12L and the applicable class definitions/rules. Sectors under s8D are not automatically Part 2B asset coverage.
Apply the constitutional/entity scope in s13 and the extraterritorial provision in s14 together with s9(2B) outside-Australia asset limitation and ss9(2C)-(2D) satellite/submarine-cable exceptions.
Use cyber security incident in s12M and unauthorised access/modification/impairment in s12N, including the actual entitlement, employee/agent scope and authorised-law-enforcement qualifications.

Report recipient is ASD under s30BF read with Definitions Rules r18. The Department is specified only for ss30BC(5) and 30BD(5) written-record exemption powers; it is not substituted as the ordinary report recipient.
The responsible entity becomes aware that a cyber security incident has occurred or is occurring.
The entity becomes aware that the incident has had or is having a significant direct or indirect impact on asset availability.

Significant impact is the if-and-only-if test in s30BEA: material disruption of essential goods/services supplied using the asset, or circumstances specified in rules. Imminence alone is not this trigger.

relationships.normative_difference: Binding Australian law, conditional on actual statutory application; the Fidelity Class is a separate governance invariant.

relationships.limitation: This supports the statutory reporting route only. It is not a pre-intrusion authorisation duty, and does not by itself prove route equivalence across every execution path.
